note:
THE SHARED CONFIGURATION PARITY CORPUS. Read by BOTH implementations: gr-uwb/lib/qa_uwb_twr_config_parity.cc (C++, the runtime authority) and gr-uwb/apps/test_twr_config.py (the retained pure-Python validator). For every case both sides must agree on the import report, the accept/reject verdict, the ORDERED list of (field, ConfigReason, ExchangeStatus) triples, the frozen effective values and the fnv1a64 config hash. The human MESSAGE of a rejection is deliberately NOT compared: the two implementations are allowed to word a rejection differently, and pinning prose would make this a string comparison rather than a contract comparison. The config hash IS compared, and it is a function of every field name, every value rendering and the order of all of them.

A 'patch' is a map of dotted path -> value applied to a deep copy of the named base document; a null value DELETES the key, which is how the missing-key cases are written. The paths are the same dotted paths the validator reports.

A non-finite double cannot be written in strict JSON and neither reader produces one, so a case that needs one names the float fields in 'non_finite_fields' and BOTH loaders assign NaN to the imported config. That post-import assignment is the only way such a value can reach a validator, and both sides do it identically. The EXHAUSTIVE sweep over every float field and all three non-finite values is generated in C++ from 'non_finite_fields' rather than listed case by case, so a new float field is covered the moment it is named and an unnamed one is a visible omission.

conventions.base: one complete, VALID config document per (protocol, role) pair
conventions.patch: dotted path -> value; null deletes the key
conventions.expect.import_ok: the verdict from the JSON reader alone
conventions.expect.effective: a subset of the frozen snapshot's values
conventions.expect.config_hash: fnv1a64 over the canonical field listing
conventions.messages_why: the human MESSAGE of a rejection is deliberately NOT compared: the Python module quotes the measured CSV cell where C++ quotes a summary, and pinning prose would turn a contract test into a string comparison. The field path, the ConfigReason and the ExchangeStatus are the contract (REQ-ERR-01).
conventions.config_hash_why: the hash is an fnv1a64 over the canonical "path=value" listing of EVERY field, so one wrong spelling, one missing entry or one field in a different order changes it. Identical hashes mean the two implementations agree on every field name, every value rendering and the order of all of them.
conventions.zero_member_why: a case whose expect.accepted is true while expect.import_ok is false is NOT a silent default: the READER refused the value and left the enumeration's zero member behind, exactly as C++ static_cast<E>(0) does, so the two implementations report the same downstream violations. The import report is the authority and is what every entry point returns.

cases.name: valid_ss_initiator
cases.note: SS-TWR, the endpoint that sends the Poll. The phase-1 common profile: ch5 / 6489.6 MHz / code 9 / 64 SYNC / 4z2 / 6.81 Mb/s payload with a 0.85 Mb/s PHR, frame v1, PHY-appends FCS, mac_psdu 32 B. Must be ACCEPTED and budget the codec's 16/26/31 on-air bytes.

cases.name: valid_ss_responder
cases.note: SS-TWR, the endpoint that answers. Same PHY, but it owns the poll_to_response reply delay and sends no Poll, so poll_start is zero.

cases.name: valid_ds_initiator
cases.note: DS-TWR, the endpoint that sends the Poll AND the Final, so it owns a non-zero response_to_final and a non-zero Final RX window.

cases.name: valid_ds_responder
cases.note: DS-TWR, the endpoint that computes the range from its own (t2B,t3B,t6B) plus the initiator's times carried in Final; it sends no Final, so response_to_final is zero and its Final RX window is armed.

cases.name: valid_sfd_4z1
cases.note: SFD mode 4z1 with its own symbol count 4. The mode names the sequence and the count is a restatement of it, never an independent number.

cases.name: valid_sfd_4z2
cases.note: SFD mode 4z2 with its own symbol count 8. The mode names the sequence and the count is a restatement of it, never an independent number.

cases.name: valid_sfd_4z3
cases.note: SFD mode 4z3 with its own symbol count 16. The mode names the sequence and the count is a restatement of it, never an independent number.

cases.name: valid_sfd_4z4
cases.note: SFD mode 4z4 with its own symbol count 32. The mode names the sequence and the count is a restatement of it, never an independent number.

cases.name: valid_sfd_decawave
cases.note: SFD mode decawave with its own symbol count 8. The mode names the sequence and the count is a restatement of it, never an independent number.

cases.name: valid_sfd_ieee
cases.note: SFD mode ieee with its own symbol count 8. The mode names the sequence and the count is a restatement of it, never an independent number.

cases.name: valid_code_10
cases.note: Preamble code 10. The joint (native_rate, code, SYNC, SFD, PSDU, ranging) lookup is all-or-nothing; codes 9..12 all have a measured row.

cases.name: valid_code_11
cases.note: Preamble code 11. The joint (native_rate, code, SYNC, SFD, PSDU, ranging) lookup is all-or-nothing; codes 9..12 all have a measured row.

cases.name: valid_code_12
cases.note: Preamble code 12. The joint (native_rate, code, SYNC, SFD, PSDU, ranging) lookup is all-or-nothing; codes 9..12 all have a measured row.

cases.name: valid_sync_16
cases.note: 16 SYNC is measured, admitted AND self-describing (preamble-duration index 0 = 16). Its first-path / ToA accuracy is still UNVERIFIED, which is a ranging-fitness caveat carried by twr_sync_reps_needing_toa_validation, not a support question.

cases.name: valid_phr_850k_with_payload_6p8m
cases.note: The exact pair M0 REJECTED: a 851.2 kb/s PHR in front of a 6.81 Mb/s payload. M0 typed phr_rate as a DataRate and required it to EQUAL data_rate, which is the inverse of what uwb_hrp_mod_core.h transmits (21 symbols of 512 chips, then 8 chips per burst of 64 per symbol).

cases.name: valid_psdu_127_boundary
cases.note: mac_psdu_bytes = 127, exactly the capability maximum (kMaxPsduBytes). Must be accepted; 128 is one case away.

cases.name: valid_psdu_29_minimum
cases.note: mac_psdu_bytes = 29, exactly the Final frame's MAC payload (14 header + 3x5 timestamps). One byte less must be rejected.

cases.name: valid_session_id_1
cases.note: The lowest legal non-zero session id. 0 is the frame profile's 'no session' marker and is refused separately.

cases.name: valid_session_id_max
cases.note: session_id = 0xFFFF, the last value the 16-bit wire field at the session offset can carry. One more must be refused, never truncated.

cases.name: valid_work_rate_quantisation
cases.note: A device-tick field quantised at the 998.4 MS/s work rate (1.0016 ns/tick), which is one of the four rates this build can express.

cases.name: valid_cg400_two_ns_budget
cases.note: 491.52 MS/s has a 2.0345 ns tick, so a 1 ns error budget is unreachable and a 2 ns one is not.  This is the CG400 counterpart of the base's UC200 (1.3563 ns tick, 1 ns budget) field, and it must be ACCEPTED with the 2 ns budget; the next case is the same field with a 1 ns budget.

cases.name: schema_v1_document_is_rejected
cases.note: A twr-config/1 document. twr-config/2 is a BREAKING change (frame.frame_profile required, phy.phr_rate changed value domain), so it must be rejected with the migration message, never silently misread: the two schemas disagree about what a PHR rate is.

cases.name: schema_unknown_version_is_rejected
cases.note: A version this build has never heard of. Generic refusal, not a migration message.

cases.name: schema_empty_is_rejected
cases.note: An empty schema_version. Required, not defaulted to the build's own.

cases.name: phr_rate_same_as_data_is_rejected
cases.note: phr_rate=same_as_data is a legal IEEE 802.15.4 / DW3xxx API option, but this build has exactly ONE PHR code path and it is the fixed 0.85 Mb/s one. The refusal is a statement about THIS SOFTWARE, not about the standard and not about any chip.

cases.name: phr_rate_payload_name_is_refused_by_the_reader
cases.note: '6p8m' is a DataRate spelling. On the phr_rate axis it is now an unknown enum value, which is the whole point of splitting the two axes. The REJECTION is the reader's; the reader leaves the enumeration's zero member behind, exactly as C++ static_cast<E>(0) does, so the subsequent verdict is 'accepted' on a field the reader already refused. The import report is the authority and is what every entry point returns.

cases.name: phr_rate_850k_spelling_is_refused_by_the_reader
cases.note: '850K' is not the accepted spelling. One spelling per member, nothing else.

cases.name: phr_rate_wrong_type_is_refused_by_the_reader
cases.note: A number where a string enum belongs.

cases.name: preamble_32_is_rejected
cases.note: Preamble length 32 SYNC: mod::encode_phr19 advertises preamble-duration index 1 (= 64) for it, so the PHR does not self-describe a 32-symbol preamble. The refusal must name a limit of THIS software and must never say a chip cannot do it.

cases.name: preamble_128_is_rejected
cases.note: Preamble length 128 SYNC: the current demodulator re-fits only the last max(40) SYNCs and synthesises earlier peaks at phase 0, so max(0, 128-64) zero-phase points leak into the CFO least-squares fit; measured at 20 kHz injected coming back as 3791 Hz. Qorvo's own API accepts 128, so this is a software limit, not a hardware one. The refusal must name a limit of THIS software and must never say a chip cannot do it.

cases.name: preamble_256_is_rejected
cases.note: Preamble length 256 SYNC: same CFO-fit bias as 128, plus the PHR advertises 64. The refusal must name a limit of THIS software and must never say a chip cannot do it.

cases.name: preamble_512_is_rejected
cases.note: Preamble length 512 SYNC: same CFO-fit bias as 128, plus the PHR advertises 64. The refusal must name a limit of THIS software and must never say a chip cannot do it.

cases.name: preamble_1024_is_rejected
cases.note: Preamble length 1024 SYNC: PHR-legal (preamble-duration index 2) but the same CFO-fit bias; measured error -19901 Hz at 20 kHz. The refusal must name a limit of THIS software and must never say a chip cannot do it.

cases.name: preamble_2048_is_rejected
cases.note: Preamble length 2048 SYNC: exceeds the work-grid TX buffer this build sizes for one frame; a buffer and scheduling decision, not a hardware capability statement. The refusal must name a limit of THIS software and must never say a chip cannot do it.

cases.name: preamble_1_is_rejected
cases.note: Preamble length 1 SYNC: leaves fewer than the 4 measured peaks stage_cfo needs. The refusal must name a limit of THIS software and must never say a chip cannot do it.

cases.name: preamble_2_is_rejected
cases.note: Preamble length 2 SYNC: leaves fewer than the 4 measured peaks stage_cfo needs. The refusal must name a limit of THIS software and must never say a chip cannot do it.

cases.name: preamble_4_is_rejected
cases.note: Preamble length 4 SYNC: shorter than the 10 initial repetitions stage_circ skips. The refusal must name a limit of THIS software and must never say a chip cannot do it.

cases.name: preamble_8_is_rejected
cases.note: Preamble length 8 SYNC: shorter than the 10 initial repetitions stage_circ skips. The refusal must name a limit of THIS software and must never say a chip cannot do it.

cases.name: preamble_100_is_rejected
cases.note: Preamble length 100 SYNC: not even in the modulator's API list, so the matrix refused to modulate it at all. The refusal must name a limit of THIS software and must never say a chip cannot do it.

cases.name: preamble_65_is_rejected
cases.note: Preamble length 65 SYNC: not a member of the PreambleLength enumeration: 16 or 64 only. The refusal must name a limit of THIS software and must never say a chip cannot do it.

cases.name: preamble_4096_is_rejected
cases.note: Preamble length 4096 SYNC: a LEGAL IEEE 802.15.4a BPRF preamble duration that this build's demodulator/CFO path still does not implement. The refusal must name a limit of THIS software and must never say a chip cannot do it.

cases.name: preamble_zero_is_a_missing_value
cases.note: preamble_symbols = 0 is 'not stated', a different rejection from 'stated and refused'.

cases.name: frame_profile_frame_v2_is_refused_by_the_reader
cases.note: 'frame_v2' is not an implemented layout, so the READER refuses it -- which is what makes 'an arbitrary profile name is an executable geometry' unrepresentable. The reader leaves frame_v1 behind, so validate() accepts a document whose import report is not empty; the import report is the authority. The validator's own profile gate is therefore reachable only for a config built in code with an out-of-enum value, and each suite exercises that path directly rather than through JSON.

cases.name: frame_profile_spelling_is_refused_by_the_reader
cases.note: 'frame_V1' is not the accepted spelling. One spelling per id.

cases.name: frame_profile_empty_is_refused_by_the_reader
cases.note: An empty profile name is not 'the default profile'; it is a missing value.

cases.name: frame_profile_missing_key_is_refused_on_import
cases.note: twr-config/2 makes frame.frame_profile REQUIRED, so its absence is a missing_key on the READER, not a later validation failure. A v1 document omitted it entirely.

cases.name: frame_profile_wrong_type_is_refused_by_the_reader
cases.note: A number where the profile enum belongs.

cases.name: phr_mode_extended_is_rejected
cases.note: phr_mode=extended asks for a vendor PHR layout longer than the 13 information bits frame v1 encodes. M0 caught only 'none' and let this through as a valid profile.

cases.name: phr_mode_none_is_rejected
cases.note: A TWR frame without a PHR is not a valid TWR profile: the PHR carries the RANGING bit and the PSDU length the receiver needs before it can decode the payload.

cases.name: phr_mode_unknown_is_refused_by_the_reader
cases.note: A PHR form outside the enumeration.

cases.name: sfd_mode_unknown_is_refused_by_the_reader
cases.note: An SFD mode outside the enumeration. The READER refuses it and leaves the enumeration's zero member (4z1 = 4 symbols) behind, which is why the subsequent verdict is a field_conflict on frame.sfd_symbols rather than a second import error.

cases.name: sfd_symbols_must_match_the_mode
cases.note: '4z2' and 4 symbols cannot both be stated: the mode names the sequence and the count is a restatement of it.

cases.name: sfd_symbols_zero_is_a_missing_value
cases.note: sfd_symbols = 0 is 'not stated', a different rejection.

cases.name: geometry_pre_m0_7_byte_header_is_rejected
cases.note: The M0 geometry: a 7-byte header (FCF 2 + seq 1 + PAN 2 + addr 2) and a 12-byte PHR. The codec emits 14 and 2. This case is the R3 defect itself: it used to be ACCEPTED with a 9/19/24-byte budget while the codec had been emitting 16/26/31 since it was frozen.

cases.name: geometry_16_byte_header_is_rejected
cases.note: A header larger than the codec's is rejected just as firmly as a smaller one: the claim does not decide the layout.

cases.name: geometry_16_byte_geometry_is_rejected
cases.note: The OTHER pre-codec geometry some M0 fixtures used. Both the 7-byte and the 16-byte header claims must fail, with the same per-field message.

cases.name: geometry_every_field_disagrees
cases.note: All five fields wrong at once. Each disagreement is its OWN rejection naming that exact field, so an operator who believes the header is 7 bytes is told it is 14 rather than handed a working config that says something else.

cases.name: geometry_timestamp_width_disagrees
cases.note: timestamp_bytes = 4 is a legal 32-bit width in the abstract but not this profile's: frame v1 declares 40 bits (REQ-TIME-04 makes the width a profile parameter, not a project-wide constant).

cases.name: geometry_not_stated_is_rejected
cases.note: An all-zero geometry. The claim must be stated explicitly and is never assumed, because assuming it is what produced the 9-byte Poll.

cases.name: geometry_missing_object_is_refused_on_import
cases.note: The whole geometry object absent. A missing object and an all-zero object are different rejections.

cases.name: geometry_mac_fcs_reserved_while_phy_appends_is_rejected
cases.note: fcs_append=phy means the modulation layer appends the FCS, so the MAC PSDU must reserve 0 FCS bytes. The authority reports it as a per-field geometry disagreement, which is the same contract as any other field.

cases.name: mac_appends_fcs_is_describable_but_not_encodable
cases.note: fcs_append=mac asks for a MAC that builds and appends the FCS itself. The geometry is DESCRIBABLE (frame_geometry_mac_appends_fcs expects the 2 FCS bytes inside the MAC PSDU) and the on-air length is unchanged, but this codec only encodes the PHY-appends form. M0 accepted such a config and then reported a MAC PSDU no encoder can produce.

cases.name: fcs_bytes_four_is_rejected
cases.note: frame v1's FCS is 2 bytes (IEEE 802.15.4). The size is the codec's, not a config field a caller chooses.

cases.name: fcs_append_none_is_rejected
cases.note: No layer appends the FCS: the frame cannot be received.

cases.name: mac_psdu_includes_fcs_conflicts_with_fcs_append
cases.note: fcs_append=phy but mac_psdu_includes_fcs=true. Exactly one layer appends the FCS, and the two fields must agree about which.

cases.name: session_id_zero_is_the_no_session_marker
cases.note: 0 is the frame profile's 'no session' marker, a different rejection from 'out of wire range'.

cases.name: session_id_0x10000_is_refused_not_truncated
cases.note: One past the 16-bit wire field. The mapping is identity-or-refuse: a lossy fold would make two different local sessions produce byte-identical session fields and the frame match would then accept the wrong session's reply as this one's (REQ-PROTO-01).

cases.name: session_id_uint32_max_is_refused_not_truncated
cases.note: The largest local session id the uint32 field can hold. It must be refused, not masked down to 0xFFFF, which is a live session id.

cases.name: mac_psdu_128_is_one_over_the_maximum
cases.note: One byte past kMaxPsduBytes = 127.

cases.name: mac_psdu_28_cannot_hold_the_final
cases.note: 28 MAC bytes cannot hold the Final frame, which needs 29 (14 header + 3x5 timestamps). The negotiated PSDU is compared against the CODEC's MAC bytes, excluding the FCS the PHY appends.

cases.name: application_payload_larger_than_the_psdu
cases.note: The application payload is a SEPARATE concept from the MAC PSDU and must fit inside it.

cases.name: channel_9_is_not_a_phase1_claim
cases.note: Channel 9 is a legal 802.15.4a channel but not a phase-1 claim: the common profile is channel 5 and other channels are per-channel acceptance items (REQ-PHY-01/03).

cases.name: channel_frequency_conflict
cases.note: Channel 5 IS 6489.6 MHz. Stating another frequency for it is a conflict, never an ignored field.

cases.name: channel_17_is_out_of_range
cases.note: The channel-plan table is 0..16.

cases.name: readback_rate_mismatch_is_a_startup_failure
cases.note: The readback native rate differs from the requested one. A mismatch is a startup failure, never a soft warning.

cases.name: cg400_one_ns_budget_is_unreachable
cases.note: 491.52 MS/s has a 2.0345 ns tick, so a 1 ns tolerated quantisation error cannot be met. Demanding it is a timing_precision_insufficient, not something to round away.

cases.name: zero_nanosecond_budget_is_insufficient
cases.note: A 0 ns tolerated error demands an exact nanosecond, which no device tick at all can express.

cases.name: quantisation_rate_this_build_cannot_express
cases.note: 2 GHz is finer than any tick this build has: not 1e9 ns, not the 998.4 MS/s work rate, not either native device rate.

cases.name: negative_quantisation_budget_is_refused
cases.note: A tolerated error may not be negative.

cases.name: reply_delay_shorter_than_the_tx_lead_time
cases.note: REQ-GR-04: a scheduled TX whose deadline cannot be met must fail, not be sent late. min_tx_lead_time has NO default; the operator supplies the measured value and a shorter reply delay is refused.

cases.name: rx_window_longer_than_the_rx_timeout
cases.note: Both are measured from the same RX enable, so a window that outlives the timeout can never complete.

cases.name: negative_delay_is_never_a_delay
cases.note: A delay may not be negative.

cases.name: calibration_id_missing
cases.note: An uncalibrated absolute range may not be claimed.

cases.name: calibration_already_applied
cases.note: A calibration is applicable EXACTLY once (REQ-CAL-01).

cases.name: calibration_channel_mismatch
cases.note: The applicability record names a different channel than phy.channel.

cases.name: calibration_profile_version_mismatch
cases.note: The calibration was taken under a different profile version.

cases.name: calibration_gain_mismatch
cases.note: The calibration was taken at a different TX gain, so it does not apply.

cases.name: calibration_record_rate_mismatch
cases.note: Calibration is versioned by sample rate; this one was taken at another rate than the radio runs.

cases.name: calibration_link_delay_unit_seconds
cases.note: The delay fields are integer nanoseconds. Mixing seconds in would be a unit mismatch, not a conversion.

cases.name: calibration_meta_version_does_not_name_the_loaded_calibration
cases.note: meta.calibration_version must name the calibration that is loaded.

cases.name: sts_sp64_is_out_of_scope
cases.note: STS is a phase-2 capability (REQ-SCOPE-04, an explicit user decision). The value exists so a future profile can claim it; phase 1 enables none of them.

cases.name: sts_sp128_is_out_of_scope
cases.note: STS is a phase-2 capability (REQ-SCOPE-04, an explicit user decision). The value exists so a future profile can claim it; phase 1 enables none of them.

cases.name: sts_sp256_is_out_of_scope
cases.note: STS is a phase-2 capability (REQ-SCOPE-04, an explicit user decision). The value exists so a future profile can claim it; phase 1 enables none of them.

cases.name: sts_sp512_is_out_of_scope
cases.note: STS is a phase-2 capability (REQ-SCOPE-04, an explicit user decision). The value exists so a future profile can claim it; phase 1 enables none of them.

cases.name: sts_sp1024_is_out_of_scope
cases.note: STS is a phase-2 capability (REQ-SCOPE-04, an explicit user decision). The value exists so a future profile can claim it; phase 1 enables none of them.

cases.name: sts_off_with_a_length_requested
cases.note: sts_mode is off but a length is asked for: the two fields disagree.

cases.name: ranging_bit_false_is_not_a_twr_profile
cases.note: REQ-PROTO-05: a TWR MAC frame must set the ranging bit.

cases.name: local_and_peer_address_identical
cases.note: Identical addresses would make every frame a match.

cases.name: report_window_is_reserved
cases.note: FrameType::Report is reserved in phase 1; a Report would invalidate the three-message interop claim.

cases.name: report_delay_is_reserved
cases.note: The final_to_report delay, same reservation as the Report RX window.

cases.name: two_in_flight_exchanges_are_refused
cases.note: Phase 1 allows at most one in-flight exchange per endpoint.

cases.name: non_finite_phy_center_frequency_hz
cases.note: NaN in phy.center_frequency_hz. No JSON document can carry a non-finite double and neither reader produces one, so the corpus names the field and BOTH loaders assign NaN to the imported config -- the only way such a value can reach a validator. It must be refused as not_finite and must never be exportable. the channel centre frequency.

cases.name: non_finite_radio_native_sample_rate_hz
cases.note: NaN in radio.native_sample_rate_hz. No JSON document can carry a non-finite double and neither reader produces one, so the corpus names the field and BOTH loaders assign NaN to the imported config -- the only way such a value can reach a validator. It must be refused as not_finite and must never be exportable. the requested native device rate.

cases.name: non_finite_rx_detection_threshold
cases.note: NaN in rx.detection_threshold. No JSON document can carry a non-finite double and neither reader produces one, so the corpus names the field and BOTH loaders assign NaN to the imported config -- the only way such a value can reach a validator. It must be refused as not_finite and must never be exportable. the coarse detection gate.

cases.name: non_finite_calibration_native_sample_rate_hz
cases.note: NaN in calibration.native_sample_rate_hz. No JSON document can carry a non-finite double and neither reader produces one, so the corpus names the field and BOTH loaders assign NaN to the imported config -- the only way such a value can reach a validator. It must be refused as not_finite and must never be exportable. the rate the calibration is versioned by.

cases.name: non_finite_calibration_record_native_sample_rate_hz
cases.note: NaN in calibration.record.native_sample_rate_hz. The applicability rule compares the record's rate against the radio rate, guarded by `> 0.0`; a NaN fails that comparison, so before M0.1 a non-finite value here skipped the validator entirely. It must be refused as not_finite like every other float field, and both sides must agree on that.
cases.note_m0_1_fix: expectation corrected from accepted=true to accepted=false: the missing finite() guard was a real defect in uwb_twr_config.h, found by the differential corpus and fixed in the same change. kFloatFieldsNotFiniteChecked is now empty. The stale effective/config_hash expectations were dropped with it.

cases.name: non_finite_timed_quantisation
cases.note: NaN in a timed field's quantisation_hz. It fails BOTH gates: not_finite, and the rate is not finite and > 0.

cases.name: non_finite_record_rate_is_a_known_gap
cases.note: NaN in calibration.record.native_sample_rate_hz. The applicability rule compares the record's rate against the radio rate guarded by `> 0.0`; a NaN fails that comparison and therefore skipped the validator entirely. M0.1 added the missing finite() guard, so this is now refused like every other float field. Both sides must agree on that.
cases.note_m0_1_fix: was a 'known gap' (accepted=true) because the C++ validator had no finiteness check on this field; found by this corpus, fixed in the same change, and re-pinned to the corrected behaviour. kFloatFieldsNotFiniteChecked is empty now.

cases.name: non_finite_several_fields_at_once
cases.note: NaN in three fields at once. Every field is reported; the report is not a list of the first problem found.

cases.name: unknown_key_is_refused_by_the_reader
cases.note: A key the schema does not define is a typo or an unsupported feature, and either way it must not be ignored. The config that comes back is otherwise the base, so the import report is the only signal.

cases.name: missing_phy_key_is_refused_on_import
cases.note: Every key of a present group is required. An absent key is a missing_key, not a default.

cases.name: fraction_where_an_integer_is_required_is_refused_by_the_reader
cases.note: A decimal fraction is never truncated silently into an integer field.

cases.name: integer_precision_loss_is_refused_on_import
cases.note: A quoted decimal that is not an int64.

cases.name: string_where_an_integer_is_required_is_refused_on_import
cases.note: The decimal-STRING form exists only for values beyond 2**53; a non-numeric string is an integer_precision_loss.

cases.name: data_rate_850k_is_refused
cases.note: The payload axis: only 6.81 Mb/s round trips, because mod::encode_phr19 hardcodes the 6.81 index and stage_payload_fcs always de-maps with the 6.81 geometry. This is the PAYLOAD axis and is a different question from the PHR rate above.

cases.name: data_rate_27m_is_refused
cases.note: Same payload axis, a different member.

cases.name: prf_class_hprf64_is_refused
cases.note: Phase 1 is a BPRF channel-5 profile; the HPRF classes are a different geometry entirely.

cases.name: code_8_is_outside_the_api_range
cases.note: radar_meta::code_index_supported() is 9..12.

cases.name: code_13_is_outside_the_api_range
cases.note: The other end of the same bound.

cases.name: tx_and_rx_codes_differ
cases.note: One profile uses one code; a mismatched TX/RX pair is a conflict, not a second profile.

cases.name: peer_claims_the_same_role
cases.note: A two-endpoint session needs one initiator and one responder.

cases.name: peer_claims_the_same_physical_channel
cases.note: One device resource, one owner (REQ-BASE-01).

cases.name: peer_shares_a_different_native_rate
cases.note: Endpoints sharing one device must share the native sample rate.

cases.name: peer_id_is_required
cases.note: A peer with no id cannot be told apart in a result.  The DUPLICATE-id rule needs two peers with one id, and the corpus base has one peer per endpoint (a two-peer document is a M1 concern), so that rule is unreachable here and is NOT claimed to be covered.

cases.name: sequence_modulus_is_not_a_power_of_two_choice
cases.note: The wrap modulus is 4, 16, 64 or 256: 2/4/6/8 sequence bits, nothing else.

cases.name: sequence_does_not_fit_the_modulus
cases.note: A sequence at or above the wrap modulus is an index error, not a value that wraps silently.

cases.name: retry_without_a_backoff
cases.note: A retry policy with more than one attempt needs a non-zero backoff, or the retries are instantaneous.

cases.name: diagnostic_budget_without_the_diagnostic
cases.note: A byte budget is stated but the diagnostic is disabled: the two fields disagree about whether anything is captured.

cases.name: diagnostic_buffer_above_the_bound
cases.note: Diagnostic memory is bounded (REQ-GR-03); this is a configure-time rejection, not a soak-time surprise.

cases.name: diagnostic_io_on_the_realtime_thread
cases.note: Diagnostic I/O must not run on the realtime processing thread (REQ-GR-02).

cases.name: device_tick_field_without_a_marker
cases.note: A device-tick field must name the RF marker it is measured at (REQ-TIME-02); the marker is what makes the number comparable with an RX timestamp.

cases.name: host_monotonic_field_with_a_marker
cases.note: There is no RF marker on a host monotonic clock, and putting one there invites a cross-domain subtraction (REQ-TIME-01).

cases.name: host_monotonic_field_requantised
cases.note: A host monotonic field must be quantised at 1e9 (integer nanoseconds).

cases.name: timed_field_reference_is_the_wrong_event
cases.note: The reference event is what makes the protocol reply delay, the post-TX RX enable delay and the RX timeout three different, non-interchangeable numbers (REQ-API-02).

cases.name: frame_tail_measured_at_the_first_rx_iq_sample
cases.note: The first RX IQ sample is not the end of a frame.

cases.name: exchange_timeout_shorter_than_the_chain
cases.note: The whole-exchange deadline must cover the chain this endpoint runs.

cases.name: measurement_interval_shorter_than_one_exchange
cases.note: At most one exchange is in flight, so consecutive measurements may not overlap.

cases.name: power_policy_names_a_field_that_is_absent
cases.note: TX gain in dB, digital IQ amplitude and calibrated antenna-plane dBm are three separate fields; naming one that is not set is a conflict.

cases.name: power_policy_untouched_with_a_value_set
cases.note: leave_untouched plus a power field is a disagreement about who authorises the power.

cases.name: calibrated_dbm_without_the_gain_it_was_measured_at
cases.note: A calibrated dBm is only meaningful together with the gain it was measured at.

cases.name: vendor_pac_value_without_a_backend
cases.note: A vendor PAC-like value is meaningless without the backend capability id that defines it, and may not be mapped onto an arbitrary software detection step.

cases.name: iq_amplitude_above_full_scale
cases.note: Digital IQ amplitude is (0, 1] for a full-scale SC16 stream.

cases.name: rx_correlation_gate_looser_than_the_detection_gate
cases.note: The fine correlation gate must not be looser than the coarse detection gate, or the fine gate is dead code.

cases.name: first_path_index_outside_the_search_window
cases.note: The first usable CIR index has to lie inside the window the search keeps.

cases.name: negative_local_address_is_a_negative_index
cases.note: local_address is a uint16 on the wire. The reader stores the int64 the JSON carried and the validator refuses it, rather than masking it to 65535 and transmitting a reserved address nobody chose.
